newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Queen Victoria statue daubed in red.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Queen Victoria statue daubed in red.

text.p: A bronze statue of former British monarch Queen Victoria, which guards the entrance to one of the British colony's biggest parks, was given a makeover on Monday with a hammer and two tins of red paint.
Police said they were called to the park after complaints that the 15-foot (4.5-metre) statue was being vandalised.
"The whole statue was covered in red paint, and its face had been dented by a hammer," police public relations officer Ken Leung told Reuters.
Leung said 27-year-old Poon Fing-lui was sitting on the statue when police arrived in response to the complaints.
But he said the man's actions had not been a political gesture related to the end of more than 150 years of British rule as Hong Kong reverts to China at midnight on June 30 next year.
"The man told police he was an artist and wanted to paint the statue," he said. "But police understand the man is mentally challenged and he has been sent to hospital for a medical examination."
The man had not been charged in connection with the incident, Leung said.
It is not the first time the statue has come to grief.
During Japan's four-year occupation of the colony during World War Two, looters took the statue for its bronze content, but it was recovered intact after liberation in 1945.
